title: Boilerplate, dickered terms, and the battle of forms
shortTitle: Boilerplate, dickered terms, and the battle of forms
summary: Boilerplate consists of standard terms reused across transactions, often while the parties separately negotiate price, quantity, or other transaction-specific matters.
notes:
The casebook describes how employees can exchange forms and perform without examining all of their conflicting standard clauses. Section 2-207 addresses one consequence in sales transactions. Notice, reasonable expectations, and unconscionability address other problems in consumer and adhesion contracts. A standard term can be binding, excluded for lack of agreement, or limited by a separate rule; its standardized form alone does not decide the result.

The casebook draws on Macaulay’s account of quotations, purchase orders, and acknowledgments. Operating personnel may check item, quantity, price, and delivery while overlooking terms drafted by lawyers or copied from other forms. This explains why section 2-207 recognizes contracts despite some differences. It does not eliminate the need for a definite expression of acceptance or make radical changes to the commercial terms irrelevant.
